title: A retract of equal-dimensional abelian varieties is an isomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety] with $\dim A=\dim B$. If homomorphisms $s:A\to B$ and $r:B\to A$ satisfy $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}_A$ as morphisms of group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], then $s$ is an isomorphism and $r=s^{-1}$.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1(c)–(d), printed p.32 (equal dimensions and finite kernel imply finite flat surjectivity), followed by the degree-one conclusion for the trivial scheme-theoretic kernel; this is the geometric completion of the one-sided inverse obtained in III Lemma 6.9, pp.106–107.

proof.text: Let $K=\ker s=A\times_{B,s,e_B}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with projections $i:K\to A$ and $p:K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $si=e_Bp$. Since $r$ is a group homomorphism, $re_B=e_A$; applying $r$ and using $rs=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives $i=e_Ap$. Because $se_A=e_B$, the pair $(e_A,\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}k})$ defines $u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to K$, with $iu=e_A$ and $pu=\mathrm{id}$. The composites $up$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$ have the same two projections: $iup=e_Ap=i$ and $pup=p$. The fibre-product universal property gives $up=\mathrm{id}_K$. Thus $p$ is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes with inverse $u$. In particular the entire scheme-theoretic kernel is finite with coordinate algebra $k$ and order $\dim_k k=1$.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, printed p.32, and scheme-theoretic kernel discussion immediately before it

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-kernel-equal-dimension-isogeny] to $s$: the hypothesis $\dim A=\dim B$ is given, and step 1 proves the required finiteness of the scheme-theoretic kernel. Consequently $s$ is surjective and finite locally free. In particular it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and surjectivity together with the finite kernel makes it an isogeny by [def-sc-isogeny].

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, printed p.32, and scheme-theoretic kernel discussion immediately before it

proof.text: Write $d=\dim_k\Gamma(K,\mathcal O_K)$, which is $1$ by step 1. Since step 2 makes $s$ an isogeny, [lem-sc-isogeny-degree] gives a locally free $\mathcal O_B$-module $s_*\mathcal O_A$ of rank $d$. Thus $r_s(b)=1$ for every point $b\in B$, not only at its identity. Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso]: step 2 supplies finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation, and the preceding equality supplies its rank hypothesis at every point. It follows that $s$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, printed p.32, and scheme-theoretic kernel discussion immediately before it

proof.text: Let $t:B\to A$ be the inverse of $s$ as a $k$-scheme isomorphism. Associativity and the two inverse identities give $r=r\mathrm{id}_B=r(st)=(rs)t=\mathrm{id}_At=t$. Therefore $sr=st=\mathrm{id}_B$, in addition to the given $rs=\mathrm{id}_A$. Both $s$ and $r$ are the original $k$-group-scheme homomorphisms, so they are mutually inverse in that category and $r=s^{-1}$.
